newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor sees internal, debt project funding.
newsitem.headline: Suncor sees internal, debt project funding.

text.p: Suncor Energy Inc expects to fund its ambitious C$2.2 billion oil sands expansion with internal cash flow and debt, not by issuing stock, Suncor Chief Executive Rick George said on Thursday.
"We have never in this company issued new equity," George told reporters in a conference call.
"I'm very worried about diluting our current shareholders. We believe we can accomplish these very aggressive goals by using our balance sheet fully and that would be our first option," he said.
When the total expansion project is completed, Suncor's assets will have doubled from today's value, George said.
Investors continued to applaud Thursday's announcement. Suncor shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange soared 6.55 to 45, a 17 percent increase, by midday.

He also said that while capital spending in the company's conventional oil and gas business and Ontario downstream operation would not be cut to fund major oil sands outlays, it would likely not increase over the next five years.

"You'll see our ongoing conventional exploration and production business be in the range between C$150 and C$200 million a year as it has been for the last three or four years, and again a very consistent kind of level in our Sunoco group," George said.
"You will not see us necessarily expand that greatly and you will not see us doing the M and A (mergers and acquisitions) kind of activity that you see other companies participating in."

Suncor earlier today announced a major phased expansion of its northern Alberta oil sands operation aimed at increasing production of synthetic light oil products to 210,000 barrels a day by 2002 from the current 85,000 barrels a day.
The spending was in addition to the company's current C$600 million expansion project.
The new Project Millennium would include expansion of oil sands extraction and upgrading facilities and acceleration of the development of Suncor's new Steepbank mine.

Suncor Vice-President Mike Ashar said the expansion plans, which dovetailed with earlier announcements of a new pipeline with partner IPL Energy Inc and an oil supply deal with Koch Oil Co Ltd, would be accomplished without acquiring new oil sands leases.
Ashar said the Steepbank mine would have a life of 25 years at a production level of 210,000 barrels a day.
